External-instrument (proxy) SVAR identification

Source: R/id-extra.R
id_proxy.Rd

id_proxy() identifies a single structural shock \(\varepsilon_{1t}\) from an external instrument \(z_t\) (Mertens & Ravn 2013; Stock & Watson 2018; Gertler & Karadi 2015). With \(u_t = s\,\varepsilon_{1t} + \dots\), the instrument satisfies relevance \(E[z_t\varepsilon_{1t}]=\phi\neq0\) and exogeneity \(E[z_t\varepsilon_{jt}]=0,\ j>1\), hence $$\gamma = E[u_t z_t] = s\,\phi,\qquad s \propto \gamma .$$ The impact vector is identified up to scale; it is normalised so that the impact response of variable target equals size: \(s = \text{size}\cdot\gamma/\gamma_{target}\). The response at horizon \(h\) is \(\Phi_h s\), \(\Phi_h\) the reduced-form MA coefficients. The estimate is the first stage of the residual on the proxy: \(\hat\gamma = T^{-1}\sum_t \hat u_t z_t\), and relevance is judged by the first-stage F of the target residual on \(z\) (see proxy_fstat()).

Usage

id_proxy(
  z = NULL,
  fit = NULL,
  gamma = NULL,
  target = 1L,
  size = 1,
  shock = target
)

Arguments

z

proxy: numeric vector of length nrow(fit$Y) (aligned with the data; first p values dropped).

fit

a varm() fit (used to compute the point gamma).

gamma

alternatively, a K vector or K x N matrix of reduced-form impact covariances (one column per reduced-form draw, as produced by proxy_draws()).

target

<tidy-select> variable whose impact response is normalised (name or position).

size

impact response of target to the shock (e.g. 0.25 for a 25bp surprise).

shock

<tidy-select> column of the IRF array that holds the proxy shock (default target).

Value

an object of class varm_id.

Details

Only column shock of the structural impact matrix is identified: the other columns of the returned IRF array are zero, so FEVD of the other shocks is meaningless (the FEVD column of the proxy shock is correct only if size is the shock standard deviation, which a proxy cannot deliver).

Uncertainty needs the data, not only \((B,\Sigma)\): use proxy_draws() which bootstraps residuals and proxy jointly and carries one \(\gamma\) per draw. Using irf(fit, id_proxy(z, fit)) with ci != "none" holds \(\gamma\) fixed and therefore understates uncertainty.

Economic intuition. A macroeconomist uses a proxy when a credible narrative/high-frequency measure of one shock is available (monetary-policy surprises around FOMC announcements, tax narratives, oil supply news) but a full recursive/sign scheme is not trusted. Pitfalls: weak instruments (F below about 10 makes the normalised IRF very wide and non-normal; use the Montiel Olea-Stock-Watson F_hac or Anderson-Rubin bands, see varm_proxy_robust()), proxy contaminated by other shocks (exogeneity), and the sample used for the proxy being shorter than the VAR (set missing proxy values to 0 only if the instrument is truly 0 there).

See also

proxy_draws(), varm_proxy()

Other identification: id_hetero(), id_restrictions(), id_zerosign(), identification, irf_fry_pagan(), proxy_draws()

Examples

fit <- varm(yraw, p = 2)
z <- c(rep(0, 2), resid(fit)[, "rate"] + rnorm(nrow(resid(fit))))
id <- id_proxy(z, fit, target = rate)
irf(fit, id, horizon = 4, ci = "none")
#> <varm IRF> K = 3, horizon 0..4, id = proxy
